claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Crypto giant Binance hit by hack suspected to be largest in history: Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
- Mushroom murderer fails to overturn convictions in Australian court challenge: Erin Patterson argued her trial was unfair due to seven grounds but three appeal judges dismissed them all.
- Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election: The PM's Likud party has alleged foreign interference and said Arab-led parties "stole" the election after his coalition lost its majority.
- Three dead after two helicopters collide midair near Oregon airport: The collision involving a Robinson R22 and an Airbus helicopter occurred on Thursday afternoon, with both aircraft crashing in a field adjacent to a highway.
- Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash: The leaked tapes appear to show one high-speed train was given clearance to move at normal speed, even though another up ahead had stalled.
- 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next: A temporary ceasefire has brought rare quiet to Kherson, offering its residents a glimpse of normal life before fighting resumes.
- Google value plunges by $500bn as AI fears rattle Wall Street: Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI search summaries were affecting ad revenue.
- Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say: At least 14 others were wounded in the attack in the central city of Dnipro, including an 11-year-old boy.
- Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss: The defeated presidential candidate says he will lead the opposition from the US.
- EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit: Ursula von der Leyen continued to use the term "associate member" for Canada despite some opposition of the bloc's members, including Germany.
- Philippine police obtain warrant to search Thomas Markle's devices: Images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Meghan's father had reportedly been found in his former home in the Philippines.
- Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports: One of the region's famous rock formations, known as "fairy chimneys", reportedly collapsed outside an open-air museum.
